$comment: THE CALIBRATION REGISTRY. Every physics constant in the engine lives here, and
every one of them carries how well it is known. Nothing in the Rust core or the
Python layer may hardcode a number that appears in this file.
WHY: this project's predecessor stalled for weeks trying to make pathfinding
match the real game. The cause was not difficulty -- it was that plausible
numbers and measured numbers were stored the same way, so a wrong guess was
indistinguishable from a fact and later tuning absorbed the error instead of
revealing it. A constant fitted to the one case anybody checked makes a wrong
LAW read as right, on every board at once.
STATUS VALUES, in increasing order of trust:
guess        nobody has evidence; a placeholder so the engine runs
hypothesis   an argument from data shape, not an observation
community    multiple independent third parties agree, no primary source
datamined    taken from shipped game data (state the file and the vintage)
measured     observed in the real game by this project's own oracle
owner_ruling a first-hand observation of the live game by a maintainer,
quoted verbatim and dated. Ranked WITH measured, never below it:
a direct observation of the live 2026 game, which is the target,
is a primary source. Added 2026-09-17, because
filing the Log ruling as 'community' would have made it
indistinguishable from the fandom prose it overturned -- exactly
the confusion this registry exists to prevent. Like measured, it
cannot be overwritten with a different value without --supersede.
A ruling may settle only PART of a key (the Log's sign, not its
off-axis vector); say which part in confidence, and keep a
promotion_rule for the rest.
PROMOTION RULE: a constant may only be promoted by adding evidence, never by
an engine result looking right. If the sim matches reality with a 'guess' in
it, that is a coincidence until measured, and saying so costs nothing.

meta.target_note: The LIVE 2026 game was chosen over a frozen 2023 build. Consequence: every datamined constant below is from 2016-2018 or 2023 game data and is therefore EVIDENCE, NOT SPEC. Supercell rewrote ground pathfinding on 2025-03-31; anything tagged pre-2025 about movement is archaeology until re-measured.

SUBTILE_PER_TILE.provenance: Design choice, following cr-sim. NOT a game constant.
rationale: This number is chosen so that it cannot bake in the answer to the two
biggest open questions (tick rate, speed divisor). Under EVERY candidate
hypothesis, a unit's per-tick displacement is an exact integer:
Speed is tiles/min, 20 TPS -> Speed * 15 subtiles/tick
Speed is tiles/min, 30 TPS -> Speed * 10 subtiles/tick
Speed is tiles/min, 60 TPS -> Speed *  5 subtiles/tick
18000 = 1000 * 18, so one millitile (the unit ALL shipped distances use)
is exactly 18 subtiles and no game data value ever needs rounding.
Consequence: we can run at 20 TPS and re-run at 60 TPS and any divergence
is a real signal rather than a rounding artefact.
SUBTILE_PER_TILE.promotion_rules: Not promotable -- it is ours, not Supercell's. Revisit only if a measured per-tick displacement is not an integer multiple of 1/18000 tile.

MILLITILE_PER_TILE.provenance: All distance columns in characters.csv/buildings.csv are millitiles. Cross-checked against community tile values across dozens of cards: Knight SightRange 5500 = 5.5 tiles, CollisionRadius 500 = 0.5, Mini P.E.K.K.A 450 = 0.45, Mortar/X-Bow Range 11500 = 11.5.
MILLITILE_PER_TILE.promotion_rules: Already as good as it gets from data and traces.

POSITION_TYPE.provenance: Community projects report entity positions as raw i32. The internal SCALE is unknown; we choose our own (above) and do not claim it matches.
POSITION_TYPE.note: Arena max is 32 tiles * 18000 = 576000, far inside i32. Squared distances reach 3.3e11 and MUST use i64 -- an i32 squared-distance is a silent overflow bug.
POSITION_TYPE.promotion_rules: Not observable in a trace; out of scope.

TICK_MS.provenance: MEASURED. OFFLINE TRACE CORPUS (Clash Royale 15.535.29 / versionCode 150535029). Traces: data/oracle-native/{walk (6 cards x 1 deploy), lane_sweep_Knight (128 files / 64 distinct experiments), building_Giant (12), repath_Giant (2), meet (3), orient (1)} -- 150 units, 51926 entity-ticks. Analysis: the offline-oracle passes -- grid, cost model, occlusion and goal rule; every law re-measured over every unit of every trace; timing and the speed law. Report: docs/movement-measurements.md; implementation contract: docs/pathfinder-spec.md. The free per-unit speed fit (no card table, S in 1..5000, synth_adjudicate B2) has exactly one survivor per card and every unit of a card fits the same integer, which only happens when one trace frame is one logic tick; at 2-5 sub-steps per tick no integer speed survives at all. The stomp pause schedule ((k+1)*TICK_MS) mod (Stop+Wait) > Stop reproduces Giant 308/308 and Golem 306/306 moving ticks with TICK_MS = 50 and no phase offset.

disagreement.30_TPS_33ms: the old engine in legacy/ used dt=0.033 (and not even exactly 1/30).

TICK_MS.why_it_matters: Every interaction is a function of this: body-block timing, whether a Fireball lands before a unit crosses, how many tower hits a Hog gets. A 3x error here is absorbed into fitted card constants and never shows up as itself.
TICK_MS.promotion_rules: SETTLED by the offline oracle. Re-open only against a second independent oracle capture, never against an argument from data shape.
TICK_MS.engine_contract: Read from here. Never write `50` in engine code.

history.provenance: No primary source exists. This is the single most load-bearing unknown in the engine.
history.overturned_by: the offline oracle ticks the battle by one logic tick per 50 ms of shipped DeployTime/HitSpeed: every measured per-tick speed is an integer number of millitiles and the stomp phase (Giant 308/308, Golem 306/306) only closes at TICK_MS = 50.

struck_2026_09_18.60_TPS_16.67ms: STRUCK. Its arithmetic is wrong: PhoenixNoRespawn DeployTime 733 ms is 733/16.667 = 43.98 ticks at 60 Hz, not 44 -- the argument needs 733.33. Lightning HitSpeed = 460 is a whole number of ticks at none of 50, 33.3 or 16.67 ms, so 'shipped durations are whole ticks' is void in either direction. Overturned by the oracle measurement above in any case.

SPEED_TO_SUBTILES_PER_TICK.units: multiplier applied to the Speed column
SPEED_TO_SUBTILES_PER_TICK.provenance: MEASURED. OFFLINE TRACE CORPUS (Clash Royale 15.535.29 / versionCode 150535029). Traces: data/oracle-native/{walk (6 cards x 1 deploy), lane_sweep_Knight (128 files / 64 distinct experiments), building_Giant (12), repath_Giant (2), meet (3), orient (1)} -- 150 units, 51926 entity-ticks. Analysis: the offline-oracle passes -- grid, cost model, occlusion and goal rule; every law re-measured over every unit of every trace; timing and the speed law. Report: docs/movement-measurements.md; implementation contract: docs/pathfinder-spec.md. Free integer per-unit fit over every moving tick of every unit (synth_adjudicate B2, no card table, S in 1..5000): exactly one survivor per card and every unit of a card fits it -- Knight 60 (131 units), Giant 52 (12), Golem 54, Skeletons 90 (3), MiniPekka 90, HogRider 120. SPEED_TO_SUBTILES_PER_TICK.why_it_matters: A flat 20% error on the movement speed of every unit in the game.
SPEED_TO_SUBTILES_PER_TICK.promotion_rules: SETTLED. The former value is in `history` and the two former hypotheses are in `struck_2026_09_18` with their original arguments, the same way time.TICK_MS archives its refuted entry -- a promotion adds evidence, it never deletes it. A buffed speed (SpeedMultiplier) follows the SAME law with a larger integer S: data/oracle-native/rage/Knight_rage_seed2.jsonl.gz fits S = 60 on t121..155, S = 78 on t156..217 (the Rage) and S = 60 again on t218..340, and 78 = 60 x 1.3 exactly. Its ROUNDING is still unmeasured, because 60 x 1.3 is a whole number and floor/round/truncate/ceil all give 78 -- see movement.STOMP_SPEED_RULE.
SPEED_TO_SUBTILES_PER_TICK.engine_contract: subtiles_per_tick = Speed * SPEED_TO_SUBTILES_PER_TICK. Set to 10 for 30 TPS, 5 for 60 TPS, 18 for the millitile-per-tick reading.

struck_2026_09_18.divide_by_60: STRUCK 2026-09-18 by the offline oracle. Its argument was: 'Speed is tiles/minute. Medium (60) = 1.00 tiles/s. Supported by cr-sim's exact-at-60TPS derivation and by the highest-sample community VOD medians (skeletons 1.56 at Speed 90, hog 1.45 at Speed 120).' struck_2026_09_18.divide_by_50: UPHELD 2026-09-18, and now measured rather than argued. Its argument was: 'Speed is millitiles per 50ms tick. Medium (60) = 1.20 tiles/s. Architecturally cleaner. Matches lower-sample VOD medians (musketeer 1.20, knight 1.12 at Speed 60).' Kept here because the entry it lived in was deleted on promotion; the evidence that settled it is in `provenance`.

PROJECTILE_SPEED_TO_SUBTILES_PER_TICK.provenance: Mirrors time.SPEED_TO_SUBTILES_PER_TICK (Speed = tiles/min at 20 TPS). Community: the AesDragon wiki blog ASSERTS (unmeasured) that projectile Speed uses the troop unit; a Darknighture frame test (2023) measured x1.2 (Speed/50) for BOTH a Musketeer projectile and a Giant. No source was found for a 'troops /50, projectiles /60' split. crforge and legacy/ use /60 for both. ARENA_SOURCE_VINTAGE.caveat: The modern client no longer ships a Map section -- the battlefield moved out of data and into code. The 2016-era per-arena data sets show TWO geometries (2-tile bridges in most arenas, 3-tile in Legendary/Royal), so bridge width is arena-dependent and possibly changed since. An 0.5-tile error in bridge span is about one Knight hitbox and decides every bridge body-block.

TERRITORY_MODEL.provenance: data/raw/retroroyale-2018/csv_logic/buildings.csv NoDeploySizeW / NoDeploySizeH, ~2018 client data (PRE-2025; evidence, not spec). The columns are set on exactly three rows: KingTower (18, 16), PrincessTower (11, 21) and NOTINUSE21, a disused copy of the king (18, 16). Carried into data/derived/cards.json towers[].no_deploy_size_tiles by tools/extract_cards.py.
TERRITORY_MODEL.rule: A TROOP may not be placed at a point inside the closed axis-aligned rectangle, centred on the tower centre with half-extents NoDeploySizeW/2 and NoDeploySizeH/2 tiles, of any ALIVE ENEMY crown tower; plus the tilemap WATER and NO_DEPLOY bits, arena bounds, building footprints, and the river band (never troop territory, see open_question). Buildings stay own half only (unsourced, unchanged). Spells anywhere.
TERRITORY_MODEL.unit_inference: TILES, inferred from 4 of 4 landmarks that come out exact under that reading and 0 of 4 under the half-tile reading, against the independently derived data/derived/arena.json and the princess tower centre (3.5, 6.5): (1) the king rect spans x = [0, 18], exactly the arena width; (2) the left and right princess rects (x = 3.5 +- 5.5 and 14.5 +- 5.5) meet exactly at x = 9, the centre line; (3) and (4) each princess rect's far edge (y = 6.5 + 10.5 = 17) is exactly the far river bank. tools/check_data.py gates all four.
TERRITORY_MODEL.consequence: With every enemy tower up, the rects forbid everything from the near river bank onward. When one enemy princess falls, the ground that opens on that side is between the far river bank (y = 17) and the enemy king rect (y = 21): 8 half-rows (4 tiles), x from the side wall to the centre line.
TERRITORY_MODEL.open_question: The four dry bridge half-columns (rows 15-17) are marked neither WATER nor NO_DEPLOY in the tilemap, so the rects alone would open them once that lane's princess falls. The engine keeps the river band closed to troops, carried from the previous rule WITHOUT a source. A recording of a troop placement attempt on the bridge after a princess tower falls settles it.

history.provenance: NONE. A pocket-depth constant in crates/royalesim/src/arena.rs: after a princess tower fell, troop territory reached 12 half-rows (6 tiles) past the far river bank on that engine-column side. Not in globals.csv, locations.csv, arenas.csv, game_modes.csv or the tilemap; chosen only to equal protocol.py MOCK_POCKET_DEPTH_HALF_ROWS. Before it, the engine used the far bank up to the destroyed tower's centre row (8.5 tiles), equally unsourced.
history.overturned_by: buildings.csv NoDeploySizeW/H on the crown towers, read as tiles: 4 of 4 arena landmarks exact (see unit_inference). The shipped mechanic replaces the depth; the depth was not tuned to 8.

TERRITORY_MODEL.promotion_rules: Record the DEEPEST legal troop placement on one lane after that lane's enemy princess tower falls (drag a troop card forward until the placement indicator refuses). This model predicts the limit at the enemy king rect edge, 4 tiles past the far river bank; the old 12-half-row model predicts 6 tiles, 2 tiles deeper. Also record whether the bridge accepts a troop then (open_question).

EXTRA_SIGHT_RANGE_TO_CROWN_TOWERS.open: Direction is ambiguous: extra range for TOWERS acquiring units, or for units acquiring TOWERS? Nobody established which.

LOGIC_RANGE_EXTENSION_TO_KEEP_TARGET.provenance: globals.csv of an UNVENDORED 2023 data, per recon. NOT PRESENT in the vendored 2018 globals.csv (data/raw/retroroyale-2018). Reported during 2026-09-12 recon as read from a newer globals.csv (a 2023 data) that this repo does not vendor, so nothing in the tree backs it. extract_globals.py lists it ABSENT on every run, deliberately.

LOGIC_PRESERVE_TARGET_IF_HIT_STARTED.meaning: Once the attack windup begins the target is locked. The old engine recomputed targets from scratch every tick with no lock at all, which silently broke every card mechanic that reads the current target.

CONTACT_LAW.provenance: SETTLED ON THE LIVE 16.402 CAPTURES on 2026-09-19/20 and VERIFIED against every one of them. The per-tick contact and locomotion update (the step, the avoidance and separation scans, the position write and the update order) is implemented in crates/royalesim/src/move16402.rs; the evidence for every rule is the live capture set. THE LAW: (1) each tick every attack update runs before every move update, and the move updates run one unit after another in CREATION order against a bucket index of collision circles (each grown by 250 for movers) built from the start-of-tick positions -- unit i sees units j < i already moved and j > i where they started (a replay with previous-tick neighbours reproduces 46 % of the contact ticks, the sequential order 98 %). (2) avoidance (states 1 and 4, not while attacking): the entities whose circle overlaps the circle of radius min(R,500) around pos + facing (facing has length 256) vote; a static (a unit that does not move) wins over movers, the last seen wins; offset 0 -> +-200, a running offset +-20 only when a static is seen, clamped to +-200, then -10 toward zero every walk tick (so 190 is the visible onset and +10/tick the visible ramp); a static whose circle contains the current waypoint's centre pops that waypoint. (3) separation (states 1, 2, 4): every overlapping neighbour of either side -- buildings and towers included, touching counts (d2 <= (R1+R2)^2; my radius capped at 500 against a static) -- adds trunc(dx x mag / d), trunc(dy x mag / d) away from it with mag = min(299, trunc(min(R1+R2-d, 300) x M_other / M_self)) + 1, and one count; coincident centres push +-1 in y by team. (4) the step: dist = max(1, isqrt(dist2)); step = min(speed, dist, 250); heading = trunc((aim - pos) << 8 / dist); step vector = trunc(heading x step / 256) per axis; facing := normalize256(aim - pos); if the offset is nonzero the step is rotated by the blend v' = ((256 - |a|) v + a perp(v)) >> 8 renormalised to the step length (tan theta = a / (256 - |a|)); the accumulator's MEAN (trunc(acc / count)) capped at 150 is added; pos += step, an axis that crosses out of the grid clamps to the cell edge, and only a DEPLOYING ground unit is clamped at a water edge; then reached := proj(aim - pos', segment) <= 1000. (5) Mass as loaded from the card data: an empty Mass column becomes tdiv(floor(R^2/250) x R, 62500) and every Mass is clamped to [1, 20] -- towers, Tombstone and Goblin Hut weigh 20, a Cannon 13, a Tesla 8 -- which is why a unit touching a tower flies back at the 150 cap. (6) With an empty path and a target out of range the unit walks at the point reach = Range + own CollisionRadius away from the target on the line to itself. VERIFICATION (over the 31 live captures, every frame pair, the world rebuilt at the start of each tick): 240389 / 242232 unit-tick positions exact (0.99239); isolated 0.99367, separation active 0.98319, two or more overlaps 0.98406, against buildings 0.99829, avoidance active 0.98221, spawn overlaps 0.99656, attacking 0.99277; the post-decay avoidance offset exact on 0.99962. The 1843 misses are diagnosed (Skeleton crowds with dying neighbours, missed stomp pauses / freezes, replanned aims, Rage inference, knockbacks not in the trace); no contact-law alternative explains more than 0.005 % of them. The Rust implementation is gated by equivalence with an independent reimplementation on random worlds (20 000 / 20 000 per seed).
CONTACT_LAW.why_it_matters: 27 % of all live moving ticks are crowded; nothing crowded reproduced before this law. Head-on units now pass each other the way the game's do.
CONTACT_LAW.promotion_rules: SETTLED by 242 232 live unit-ticks. Re-open only against a new client build.
CONTACT_LAW.engine_contract: state.rs phase_path16402 runs it under pathfinding.PATH_SEARCH = client16402 (the same arm that selects the measured 16.402 search): units update one after the other in creation order, the position write is the game's, collide::separate and the river ejection are bypassed. The frame-planned arm keeps the engine's own guessed separation (PUSH_MODEL below).

movement.CONTACT_DOMAIN = isolated_unit_only (the domain of the trace-fitted arm's locomotion law; under this law every unit-tick is in domain)
open: knockback (confirmed live: speed ladder 25n, -25 per tick, one back-step) is not modelled; the engine still runs its fixed_distance slide

the JumpEnabled water hop, the dash and jump states, the touchdown/capture-mode branches
the death order inside one move pass (a unit killed by an earlier mover's attack component is dropped from later scans in the same tick; measured, mechanism not read)

PUSH_MODEL.provenance: NONE. The data ships a Mass column (Skeleton 1, Knight 6, Giant 18, Golem 20) and the wiki says mass matters qualitatively -- but a field existing is not a formula, and the best public reimplementation ignores Mass entirely and weights by speed ratio instead.
PUSH_MODEL.why_it_matters: Unit push governs body-blocking, swarm spread, and whether a tank walks through or around its own support -- i.e. most of what a player is actually doing. The old engine had NO unit collision whatsoever, which is the single biggest reason it could not model the game.
PUSH_MODEL.promotion_rules: Directly measurable from captures: record scripted head-on collisions across a mass ladder (Skeleton 1 / Knight 6 / Giant 18 / Golem 20) and a speed ladder, then fit the displacement ratio against mass-ratio, speed-ratio and the product. Also check for a per-tick displacement cap, which is invisible in aggregate.
PUSH_MODEL.oracle_note_2026_09_18: NOTHING RECORDS THE PUSH. It is not separately observable in the offline-oracle corpus -- it must be fitted from the movement RESIDUAL (movement.CONTACT_DOMAIN): |step| about S plus a 15-28 unit lateral residual perpendicular to the heading for crowd separation, and 0.06-2.5 x S, possibly opposing the heading, for combat pushback. BUILDING_FOOTPRINT_MODEL.provenance: Three candidate models disagree for exactly the cases that decide games. The King Tower's shipped no-deploy block is 3x3 tiles but its CollisionRadius is 1400 (2.8 tiles diameter) -- those do not reconcile. Princess towers are NOT in the static map at all, so their footprint must come from CollisionRadius 1000 (a 2x2 box), which contradicts the commonly-quoted 3x3.
BUILDING_FOOTPRINT_MODEL.why_it_matters: Decides whether a unit can squeeze between a princess tower and the arena edge, and where a melee unit stands to hit a tower.
BUILDING_FOOTPRINT_MODEL.promotion_rules: Walk a minimum-radius unit (CollisionRadius 400) along a tower edge and record closest approach. Repeat for king and princess.

ALGORITHM.provenance: MEASURED. OFFLINE TRACE CORPUS (Clash Royale 15.535.29 / versionCode 150535029). Traces: data/oracle-native/{walk (6 cards x 1 deploy), lane_sweep_Knight (128 files / 64 distinct experiments), building_Giant (12), repath_Giant (2), meet (3), orient (1)} -- 150 units, 51926 entity-ticks. PATH_SEARCH.provenance: SETTLED ON THE LIVE 16.402 CAPTURES on 2026-09-19 and verified against every first path they publish (three independent reproductions of the search agree on every rule below). Every tie-break below was chosen because it reproduces the published node lists, not because a different order was ruled out by argument. The rules cover the search and the path request that enters it, the expansion and relaxation, the heuristic, the cell cost, the building box, the per-tick occlusion rebuild, and the move component's goal-cell choice. THE RULES: (1) ONE goal cell, chosen by the move component: scan rows ascending over target_cell +- (reach/500 + 1), columns ascending when the mover's x < 9000 native else descending, keep the highest category (2 = dry and outside every building box, 1 = water or boxed) and within it the strictly smallest squared distance to the MOVER (first scanned wins ties); reach = Range + own CollisionRadius. (2) the cell cost: -1 out of bounds only; water (tilemap bit 0x20) costs BLOCKED = 50 for a walker and is priced, not refused; no cell of the arena tilemap sets bit 0x40; lane bits & 3 cost ROAD = MATCHINGROAD = 5; else DEFAULT 8; then max(base, occlusion[cell]) where every building of BOTH sides stamps BUILDING = 50 over the half-open box [c - R, c + R) after snapping its centre UP to the next multiple of 500 on each axis, and a box that does not fit entirely inside the grid stamps nothing. Bit 16 plays no part in the cell cost; the king block is priced by the king's own R = 1400 box. (3) step cost = entered cell's cost x 10, x 14 on a diagonal (integer); h = 5 x (10 max(|dc|,|dr|) + 4 min(|dc|,|dr|)) (HEURISTIC_METHOD 1, times DEFAULTHEURISTIC_COST 5); f = g + h. (4) among equally cheap routes, the published route is the one an open list ordered on f alone (no g, no h, no insertion order) produces when equal keys keep their existing order. (5) neighbours in the order N, S, W, E, NW, SW, SE, NE; the start is expanded before the loop; a popped cell is closed, expanded, and the loop ends when the GOAL is closed (i.e. after it has been popped and expanded). (6) an open node reached with a strictly better f takes the new parent, g and f (REFRESH_OPENNODES); a closed node is never revisited (REOPEN_CLOSEDNODES = FALSE). (7) the published list is the parent chain from the goal, goal first, without the start cell. VERIFICATION (scored against the captures): 435/438 live 16.402 first paths and 128/128 offline 15.535 lane-sweep paths reproduce the exact published node sequence; the three live misses are Goblins chasing a MOVING target whose goal cell the trace cannot recover (the sample's target position is the previous tick's). The trace-fitted arm scored 168/345 and 15/128. Controls run on the same harness: water impassable instead of priced 306/388 and 24/128; friendly-only occlusion 336/388; KS_POS_TO_TARGET_GROUND_AVOID_BUILDINGS off 421/425. See docs/pathfinding.md.

HEURISTIC_FORM.formula: h(cell) = min over the GOAL SET of PATHFINDING_DEFAULTHEURISTIC_COST * max(|dc|, |dr|), i.e. 5 * Chebyshev, with the goal set unchanged (see why_the_goal_set).
HEURISTIC_FORM.provenance: MEASURED. LIVE CLIENT, CR 16.402 -- recorded from the real game and converted to the offline-oracle trace format; 13 captures. Analysis: the expansion pass (exact node-sequence reproduction; corpus 337 first paths, 292 after de-duplicating the two two-client pairs). Report: the live 16.402 measurements. HANDED THE ORACLE'S OWN GOAL CELL, exact node-sequence reproduction: the engine's shipped ortho-first + octile 78/292; Dijkstra (h = 0) 171/292; forward A* with strict-< relaxation, entered-cell costs and h = W * max(|dc|, |dr|) for W in 3..5, 192/292 (65.8 %). Offline, the same sweep on lane_sweep_Knight reads 36/128 for Chebyshev against 14/128 for ortho-first + octile, so this is not a 16.402 change -- it is a better fit on both builds. THE WEIGHT IS NOT PINNED: W = 3, 4 and 5 are indistinguishable on this corpus; 5 is taken because it is the shipped PATHFINDING_DEFAULTHEURISTIC_COST, a datamined constant that fits rather than a fitted one. With the reach PREDICATE as the goal test instead of the handed goal cell the best falls to 142/292, which is the goal-cell question (PATH_GOAL_RULE `limits`), not the heuristic's.
HEURISTIC_FORM.admissibility: 5 * Chebyshev is admissible and consistent against this cost field, so REOPEN_CLOSEDNODES = FALSE stays safe and the returned path is still exactly cost-minimal. The cheapest cell costs road = 5 to enter and the cheapest diagonal 5 * 1414/1000 = 7, so a route of Chebyshev distance N costs at least 5N; and h changes by at most 5 across any neighbour while a diagonal step costs at least 7. crates/royalesim/src/path2026.rs `the_measured_heuristic_is_chebyshev_and_both_forms_are_admissible` asserts the consequence directly -- swapping the form may not change what a path COSTS.
HEURISTIC_FORM.why_the_goal_set: ADMISSIBILITY TRAP, and it is not cosmetic. THIS HALF IS UNCHANGED BY THE 16.402 PROMOTION -- only the metric inside the minimum changed. The goal is 'any cell within reach of the target' (PATH_GOAL_RULE), so a heuristic computed to the TARGET cell over-estimates the cost to the actual goal by up to reach/500 * 5 and is non-zero at goal cells -- A* then pops a goal that is not the cheapest one. Measured on the walk traces: with h to the target cell the search returns column 7 (cost 152) instead of the oracle's column 6 (cost 150) for every one of the six cards; with h as the min over the in-reach cells it returns the oracle's path.
HEURISTIC_FORM.still_not_reproduced: The heuristic does not change WHICH paths are optimal (the cost model was validated with Dijkstra), only the expansion order. 192/292 is a ceiling, not a solution: the residual has one systematic signature -- the oracle shifts column one cell EARLIER than the model, always immediately after a road/bridge segment (witnesses 20260918-112215:25:MiniPekka and 20260918-112751:7:Giant both 8,33 -> 7,32 -> 7,31 -> 8,30 where the model stays 7,30; 112751:32:Musketeer 5,39 -> 6,38 vs 5,38). A heuristic charging more than the 11-vs-8 diagonal premium for a one-column offset would produce it, but every b - a >= 4 member of h = a*(max-min) + b*min scores far worse overall. It may not be a heap A* at all: a different heuristic form, a post-processing pass over the raw route and a hierarchical search are all still live. Keep it swappable.

TIE_BREAK.provenance: UNVERIFIED AND KNOWN TO BE INSUFFICIENT. Where several successors are equally optimal the oracle prefers the orthogonal one on 1568 of 1672 ambiguous steps (93.8 %), but an ortho-first neighbour order still reproduces only 22/140 exact node sequences, and with the sqrt(2) diagonal exact ties are rare -- so the residual divergence is not a classic tie-break at all. 76 distinct experiments over neighbour order x queue discipline x relaxation rule; none exceeds 13/76. OFFLINE TRACE CORPUS (Clash Royale 15.535.29 / versionCode 150535029). Traces: data/oracle-native/{walk (6 cards x 1 deploy), lane_sweep_Knight (128 files / 64 distinct experiments), building_Giant (12), repath_Giant (2), meet (3), orient (1)} -- 150 units, 51926 entity-ticks. TIE_BREAK.why_it_may_be_unreachable: The recorded path_nodes is a POST-TICK snapshot: a repath can insert one or two nodes below the old waypoint that the unit aims at and consumes within the same tick, so they appear in no recorded frame. 142 ticks in the corpus show this; all carry path_node_consumed == 1 and 140 are explained exactly by a cell 1-2 rows nearer in the same column. Any pathfinder fitted to the recorded node lists is missing those insertions.
TIE_BREAK.why_the_knob_provably_cannot_matter: LIVE 16.402, the expansion sweep over the live corpus: 36 combinations of 6 open-list keys x 6 neighbour orders produce ZERO different paths across 418 samples. The reason is structural, not statistical -- with strict-`<` relaxation and an f-first heap, rival parents of a cell differ in g by 2, 3 or 6 while their h differs by 0 or one cell-weight, so an f-tie between them essentially never occurs and the neighbour order never gets a vote. The offline 1040-configuration sweep therefore had at most ~5 genuinely distinct members. THE VALUE STAYS A PLACEHOLDER AND IT IS A HARMLESS ONE; the note below that 'the three orders give a DIFFERENT path on only 25 of 6802 engine problems' is the same fact measured on the engine's own grid. Whatever settles the expansion order will have to change the open-list key or the algorithm, not the neighbour list -- and the leading suspects are now the HEURISTIC (promoted to chebyshev_over_goal_set on the same corpus, 78/292 -> 192/292) and the possibility that it is not a heap A* at all.
TIE_BREAK.promotion_rules: Do not record a tie-break as settled on this corpus. Settle it with a scenario whose optimum is unique but whose EXPANSION order is observable, or by the measured 16.402 search itself (PATH_SEARCH = client16402 settles it). Note that a scenario cannot settle it while the relaxation stays strict-`<`: see why_the_knob_provably_cannot_matter.
TIE_BREAK.engine_contract: royalesim reads this key into Calib::tie_break and path2026.rs `neighbours()` SELECTS the neighbour order from it -- the three candidates above are the three the engine implements, and Calib::from_json refuses any other name. It used to be read and then ignored, with one hardcoded order underneath, so two of the three values named a discipline that never ran. MEASURED while wiring it: the neighbour order reaches the result ONLY through the push counter in the open-list key (f, then the smaller h, then FIFO), so over a 6802-problem sweep on the shipped grid the three orders give a DIFFERENT path on only 25, and never a different cost. Whatever settles spec 3.6 will therefore have to change the open-list key, not just the neighbour list (path2026.rs `OpenKey`). The two candidates cw_from_n / ccw_from_n were dropped from this list because the engine does not implement them; add them back together with their arms.

OCCLUDED_CELL_TREATMENT.scope: APPLIES TO BUILDING OCCLUSION BOXES ONLY -- never to water, and, since 2026-09-18, no longer to bit-16 terrain either. WATER: the two used to share one branch in path2026.rs `CostField::terrain`, so selecting `cost_50` here silently made the river traversable and overrode WATER_RULE_GROUND, which Calib::from_json refuses to load with any value but `impassable`. BIT-16: the same defect, one key deciding another's question -- `cost_50` is a statement about BUILDINGS and it used to make the deploy-restricted arena-edge strips walkable as a side effect. path2026.rs `CostField::terrain` now writes the goal-exempt OCCLUDED sentinel for bit 16 unconditionally and `CostField::occlude` overwrites it with the box cost where the two overlap (see precedence). One ledger key may not quietly override another.
OCCLUDED_CELL_TREATMENT.precedence: THE BOX COST TAKES PRECEDENCE OVER THE TERRAIN FLAG, and that is the actionable finding -- neither analysis stated it, and their apparent disagreement about bit 16 was entirely this. A bit-16 cell inside a building box costs 50 like any occluded cell. An engine that resolves terrain FIRST and lets an impassable bit-16 flag win costs 39 of 337 live paths, because the tilemap's bit-16 king 3x3 block IS the king tower's own R = 1400 half-open box, cell for cell. Live paths use 744 distinct cells, of which 13 carry bit 16 and ALL 13 lie inside a king box; the other 104 bit-16 cells (the arena-edge strips) are never entered by any path, and no live path touches water anywhere. So bit 16 has no measurable pathfinding meaning of its OWN -- impassable, 5, 8, 12, 50 and 1000 all score 6/785 once enemy occlusion is on -- and spec rule 2.2 is NOT refuted. It is kept impassable outside every box as the conservative reading of an unidentifiable flag.
OCCLUDED_CELL_TREATMENT.engine_contract: royalesim reads this into Calib::occluded_cells (state.rs) and path2026.rs `CostField::occlude` selects the value it stamps: PATHFINDING_BUILDING_COST under `cost_50`, the goal-exempt OCCLUDED sentinel under `block`. Both candidates are wired and a name with no arm is refused at load. The SHAPE is kept separately from the cost -- `CostField::in_building_box` answers 'is this cell inside a box' whichever treatment is selected -- because under `cost_50` nothing is refused and every gate that asked `refused` would have passed vacuously.
OCCLUDED_CELL_TREATMENT.goal_cell_exemption: SPEC 4.6 BECOMES UNNECESSARY, and deleting it is an improvement. 456 of 785 live goal cells sit inside a building box, so under the old hard-block reading the exemption was load-bearing; under cost 50 it can go and the score IMPROVES -- 6 failures without it against 12 with it, otherwise identical settings. In royalesim the exemption is now unreachable for building boxes (they are a price, not the sentinel) and survives only on the bit-16 king block, where it is what keeps a short-reach card able to path to a king tower at all and where the live corpus cannot see it either way (path2026.rs OCCLUDED).

WATER_RULE_GROUND.provenance: MEASURED. OFFLINE TRACE CORPUS (Clash Royale 15.535.29 / versionCode 150535029). Traces: data/oracle-native/{walk (6 cards x 1 deploy), lane_sweep_Knight (128 files / 64 distinct experiments), building_Giant (12), repath_Giant (2), meet (3), orient (1)} -- 150 units, 51926 entity-ticks. Analysis: the offline-oracle passes -- grid, cost model, occlusion and goal rule; every law re-measured over every unit of every trace; timing and the speed law. Report: docs/movement-measurements.md; implementation contract: docs/pathfinder-spec.md. PATHFINDING_WATER_COST = 7 is in the shipped globals but it is WRONG for ground: modelling water as traversable at cost 7 makes 25 of 150 oracle first paths strictly dearer than the optimum -- the oracle refused water shortcuts it would have taken. Water at cost 50 and a hard block are indistinguishable; the hard block is taken for ground and cost 7 is left available for whatever it is really for (flyers, or a non-pathfinding use).
WATER_RULE_GROUND.engine_contract: path2026.rs `CostField::terrain` writes the IMPASSABLE sentinel for the water bit unconditionally, and path2026.rs `plan_cells` refuses it WITHOUT the spec-4.6 goal exemption -- a distinct sentinel from OCCLUDED, which the goal cell may use. Sharing one sentinel extended the exemption to the river: a ground unit whose target stands on a bridge has in-reach cells two rows into the water, and the route's final cell could legally be one of them. No trace exercises it, so no gate caught it.

PATH_GOAL_RULE.provenance: MEASURED. OFFLINE TRACE CORPUS (Clash Royale 15.535.29 / versionCode 150535029). Traces: data/oracle-native/{walk (6 cards x 1 deploy), lane_sweep_Knight (128 files / 64 distinct experiments), building_Giant (12), repath_Giant (2), meet (3), orient (1)} -- 150 units, 51926 entity-ticks. Analysis: the offline-oracle passes -- grid, cost model, occlusion and goal rule; every law re-measured over every unit of every trace; timing and the speed law. Report: docs/movement-measurements.md; implementation contract: docs/pathfinder-spec.md. The path is truncated at the FIRST cell whose CENTRE is within Range + CollisionRadius of the TARGET'S CENTRE POINT -- the target's centre, not its footprint, and not the sum of both collision radii. Verified two-sided (the goal is in reach AND its predecessor is out of reach) on 150/150 first paths, including the meet/ traces with moving targets and side-1 units. Rivals: 'Range only' 1/140, 'Range + both radii' 0/140, 'footprint edge' 0/140. Per-card stop cells from one deploy tile: Giant (reach 1950) row 47; Knight 1700, Golem 1500, HogRider 1400 all row 48; MiniPekka 1250 and Skeletons 1000 row 49.
PATH_GOAL_RULE.limits: NECESSARY, NOT DETERMINATIVE. It is a condition on the last node, not a predictor of which cell the search stops at: between 12 and 52 cells per sample satisfy it (median 32) and the oracle's goal cell is not the cheapest reachable in-reach cell in 114 of 140 samples, with no cost ties among them. Handing an A* the oracle's goal cell raises exact-sequence reproduction from 22/140 to 43/140 -- THE GOAL CELL IS AN OUTPUT OF THE EXPANSION ORDER. Implement the reach test as the goal PREDICATE and let the pop order choose; do not implement 'pick the nearest or cheapest in-reach cell'. A constant k added to Range + CollisionRadius fits all 150 paths for any k in [-125.2, +24.8), so the reach is pinned to about +-75 units, not exactly.
PATH_GOAL_RULE.sign: The standoff is on the APPROACH side, not unconditionally negative in y: in meet/Knight_vs_HogRider ticks 250-273 the Knight's target is BELOW it and the goal row is cell_centre_y + reach. An unconditional minus puts the goal on the far side of the target. The predicate form (a radius about the target centre) carries this for free.
PATH_GOAL_RULE.cadence: Re-derive the goal cell every tick and replan only when the resulting CELL changes (REPLAN_TRIGGERS): that reproduces the 137 observed goal-driven replans with the observed 1-2 tick lag.

WAYPOINT_ARRIVE_RADIUS.provenance: MEASURED. OFFLINE TRACE CORPUS (Clash Royale 15.535.29 / versionCode 150535029). Traces: data/oracle-native/{walk (6 cards x 1 deploy), lane_sweep_Knight (128 files / 64 distinct experiments), building_Giant (12), repath_Giant (2), meet (3), orient (1)} -- 150 units, 51926 entity-ticks. Analysis: the offline-oracle passes -- grid, cost model, occlusion and goal rule; every law re-measured over every unit of every trace; timing and the speed law. Report: docs/movement-measurements.md; implementation contract: docs/pathfinder-spec.md. At most ONE node is consumed per tick: 0 of 3851 tail-drop ticks dropped more than one. Threshold sweep on the post-move Euclidean distance: 1000 is the one-sided exact value (zero false drops across 27824 keep-ticks); 1001 buys 27 fewer misses and costs 3 false drops, 1003 gives 107 total against 148, 1005 and beyond are worse. NOT TUNED to hide the residual -- see WAYPOINT_ARRIVE_RULE, which explains it instead.

candidate_meanings.segment_projection: Consume the tail node when the REMAINING DISTANCE ALONG THE SEGMENT, dot(node_centre - post_move_position, segment_direction) / 256 with integer truncation, is <= WAYPOINT_ARRIVE_RADIUS. segment_direction is the 1/256 unit vector frozen when the node was assigned (norm256(node_centre - POST-move position), the engine's own path_segment_direction field).
candidate_meanings.euclid_post_move: the pathfinder spec's rule 7.5 as written: consume when the post-move EUCLIDEAN distance (floored integer sqrt) to the node centre is <= WAYPOINT_ARRIVE_RADIUS.

WAYPOINT_ARRIVE_RULE.provenance: MEASURED, and it SUPERSEDES the spec's rule 7.5 on the same corpus. OFFLINE TRACE CORPUS (Clash Royale 15.535.29 / versionCode 150535029). Traces: data/oracle-native/{walk (6 cards x 1 deploy), lane_sweep_Knight (128 files / 64 distinct experiments), building_Giant (12), repath_Giant (2), meet (3), orient (1)} -- 150 units, 51926 entity-ticks. Analysis: the offline-oracle passes -- grid, cost model, occlusion and goal rule; every law re-measured over every unit of every trace; timing and the speed law. Report: docs/movement-measurements.md; implementation contract: docs/pathfinder-spec.md. Scored over all 34644 stable-list tick pairs (3975 ordinary drops, 30669 keeps) (reproduced by tools/oracle_diff.py --rule): euclid_post_move misses 153 drops and fires 3 times early (156 errors); segment_projection misses 6 and fires 10 times early (16 errors), and ALL TEN of its early fires carry avoidance_offset != 0 (110, 190, 150, 140, 130, -160) -- the avoidance regime that is outside the domain of every movement law here (CONTACT_DOMAIN). On the walk family (the isolated-unit gate) segment_projection has ZERO errors; euclid_post_move misses 4, which is exactly why the spec expected '~4 % of pop ticks to diverge'. The mechanism it adds was already in the spec as rule 7.7 -- the segment direction is frozen at consumption and held for the whole segment, zero exceptions on the walk traces -- it was simply never connected to the consumption predicate.
WAYPOINT_ARRIVE_RULE.disproof_of_a_pure_radius: No radius on the post-move distance can be right: restricted to ISOLATED units (single-unit traces, avoidance_offset == 0, behavior_state == 1) the Knight corpus contains a DROP at distance 1004.478 and a KEEP at 1000.648, so drops and keeps overlap in distance. They do not overlap in the projection.
WAYPOINT_ARRIVE_RULE.engine_contract: royalesim stores the frozen direction per entity (entity.seg_dir) and evaluates the predicate AFTER the move, at most one pop per tick (state.rs phase_path_2026). Setting this key to euclid_post_move runs the spec's rule 7.5 instead.

GENERATOR.provenance: Supercell's own PRNG has never been recovered publicly. A real replay is a function of a single rndSeed int, so the generator is a REQUIRED component of reproducing a real match -- and an unavailable one.
GENERATOR.consequence: We cannot replay a real recorded match. We CAN guarantee bit-identical reproducibility within our own build, which is a different and entirely attainable property, and the one every test depends on.
GENERATOR.engine_contract: The RNG is owned by battle state and its bit-state is part of the serialized state. A replay is seed + action log + periodic state hash. The old engine had 23 module-global `random` call sites and zero occurrences of `seed`, so nothing it produced was reproducible at all.

$comment: THE PER-TICK LOCOMOTION LAW OF A GROUND TROOP, measured from the offline oracle on
2026-09-18. Order matters: re-derive the goal cell, replan if it moved, apply the
stomp pause, take the heading from the PRE-move position, step with per-axis
truncation, then consume at most one waypoint. Permuting it does not reproduce the
traces.
EVERY LAW HERE HAS A DOMAIN: CONTACT_DOMAIN. They hold for a unit that is not in
contact with another unit. Two of the three regimes that break them set no flag at
all, so an engine that fits card constants to crowded traces will absorb the
avoidance and separation terms into the wrong place.

HEADING_LAW.formula: d = node_centre - position (PRE-move); L = floor(sqrt(d.x^2 + d.y^2)); dir = (d.x * 256 / L, d.y * 256 / L) with integer division truncating toward zero
HEADING_LAW.provenance: MEASURED. OFFLINE TRACE CORPUS (Clash Royale 15.535.29 / versionCode 150535029). Traces: data/oracle-native/{walk (6 cards x 1 deploy), lane_sweep_Knight (128 files / 64 distinct experiments), building_Giant (12), repath_Giant (2), meet (3), orient (1)} -- 150 units, 51926 entity-ticks. Analysis: the offline-oracle passes -- grid, cost model, occlusion and goal rule; every law re-measured over every unit of every trace; timing and the speed law. Report: docs/movement-measurements.md; implementation contract: docs/pathfinder-spec.md. 100 % on every isolated unit. The FLOORED length is what is load-bearing, not the sqrt routine: over 1258 walk ticks floor(sqrt) matches 1258, nearest-integer 1179, scale-then-sqrt 191, ceil 173. The PRE-move position as the origin scores 106-307 ticks per card against 85-264 for post-move.
HEADING_LAW.do_not: |dir| legitimately ranges 254.678..256.236 because each axis truncates independently -- DO NOT renormalise or clamp to 256. Heading is STATELESS: a pure function of position and current node, recomputed from scratch. No inertia, no angular smoothing, no turn-rate limit; it snaps 71.57 degrees in one tick on a spawn tick and nothing in the corpus exceeds that. RotateAngleSpeed exists as a card column but only turret-like cards set it (cannon_cart, zapmachine, minizapmachine, dartbarrell) -- none is a troop.

POSITION_ROUNDING.formula: position.x += trunc(S * dir.x / 256); position.y += trunc(S * dir.y / 256)
POSITION_ROUNDING.provenance: MEASURED. OFFLINE TRACE CORPUS (Clash Royale 15.535.29 / versionCode 150535029). Traces: data/oracle-native/{walk (6 cards x 1 deploy), lane_sweep_Knight (128 files / 64 distinct experiments), building_Giant (12), repath_Giant (2), meet (3), orient (1)} -- 150 units, 51926 entity-ticks. Analysis: the offline-oracle passes -- grid, cost model, occlusion and goal rule; every law re-measured over every unit of every trace; timing and the speed law. Report: docs/movement-measurements.md; implementation contract: docs/pathfinder-spec.md. The sub-unit remainder is DISCARDED every tick: integrating this law alone from the first moving tick reproduces the final position exactly over 106-308 ticks with zero drift. Floor matches 0 of about 1000 discriminating ticks (dir.x < 0 on every moving tick of every walk unit, so floor and truncation differ on every one); round matches 17-43 per card; ceil 201/240.
POSITION_ROUNDING.engine_contract: Rust i32/i32 already truncates toward zero and is correct. Do NOT use f32 and do NOT use div_euclid. The pre-2026 models keep path::advance's 1/65536 fractional carry -- that carry is WRONG for this model and is not used by it.

STOMP_SPEED_RULE.formula: S = Speed if StopMovementAfterMS is unset, else floor(Speed * (StopMovementAfterMS + WaitMS) / StopMovementAfterMS)
STOMP_SPEED_RULE.rounding_2026_09_18b: THE ROUNDING IS FLOOR, MEASURED, which is what raises this key from MEDIUM to HIGH. MEASURED on the LIVE 16.402 client (the live corpus, 13 captures; the movement analysis, Ice Golem arm). The Giant and the Golem could never separate it -- 45 * 740/640 = 52 and 45 * 1200/1000 = 54 are whole numbers, so floor, round and truncate all agree and only ceil was excluded. THE ICE GOLEM SEPARATES IT: icegolemite.toml ships Speed 45, StopMovementAfterMS 470, WaitMS 80, and 45 * 550/470 = 52.6596. Over 2373 ISOLATED free-walk moving ticks, S = 52 scores 2231, S = 53 scores 29, S = 51 scores 104 and S = 54 scores 0. Floor. royalesim already computed floor -- card.rs `move_speed` is integer division on non-negative operands -- so this promotion adds evidence and changes no behaviour.
STOMP_SPEED_RULE.provenance: MEASURED as a value, PARTLY UNVERIFIED as a formula. OFFLINE TRACE CORPUS (Clash Royale 15.535.29 / versionCode 150535029). Traces: data/oracle-native/{walk (6 cards x 1 deploy), lane_sweep_Knight (128 files / 64 distinct experiments), building_Giant (12), repath_Giant (2), meet (3), orient (1)} -- 150 units, 51926 entity-ticks. Analysis: the offline-oracle passes -- grid, cost model, occlusion and goal rule; every law re-measured over every unit of every trace; timing and the speed law. Report: docs/movement-measurements.md; implementation contract: docs/pathfinder-spec.md. The free per-unit fit gives Giant 52 and Golem 54 while their Speed column is 45 for both; 640/100 and 1000/200 are their shipped StopMovementAfterMS/WaitMS. It is a TWO-POINT fit: Speed + floor(Speed*Wait/Stop) agrees on every shipped stomp card. The offline corpus cannot identify the rounding mode -- floor, round and truncate all give Giant 52 / Golem 54, and only ceil is excluded -- but the live Ice Golem can, because its value is not a whole number: it reads 52 rather than 53, so the rounding is FLOOR. The formula itself is still a two-point fit on the SHAPE; what is settled is the rounding.
STOMP_SPEED_RULE.do_not: Do NOT apply WalkingSpeedTweakPercentage to movement -- it is animation only (the Golem carries both a 15 % tweak and a stop/wait, and 45 * 1.15 = 51.75 != 54). S is the UNBUFFED base.
STOMP_SPEED_RULE.cards: Shipped stomp cards: Giant 640/100, RoyalGiant 640/100, Golem 1000/200, IceGolemite 470/80, GoblinGiant (2026 only). Extracted into data/derived/cards.json as stop_movement_after_ms / wait_ms.
STOMP_SPEED_RULE.buffed_speed: MOVED to movement.BUFF_SPEED_RULE, which is now its own measured key -- the live corpus separated its rounding too. What stood here: 'CORRECTED 2026-09-18 (this key used to say a buffed speed was unmeasured because no trace has one; one does). data/oracle-native/rage/Knight_rage_seed2.jsonl.gz drops a Rage at tick 140. Fitting the free integer S of movement.POSITION_ROUNDING over the Knight's isolated ticks (behavior_state == 1, avoidance_offset == 0) gives S = 60 on t121..155, S = 78 on t156..217 and S = 60 again on t218..340: the buffed regime is the SAME law with a larger integer S, held for 62 ticks, and 78 = 60 x 1.3 exactly. WHAT IS STILL UNMEASURED IS THE ROUNDING, for the same reason as the stomp formula above: 60 x 1.3 is a whole number, so floor, round, truncate and ceil all give 78.'

BUFF_SPEED_RULE.formula: S_buffed = floor(S * SpeedMultiplier / 100), where S is the speed the unit ALREADY walks at (i.e. the STOMP_SPEED_RULE output for a stomp card, not the raw Speed column) and SpeedMultiplier is a property of the BUFF
BUFF_SPEED_RULE.provenance: MEASURED. LIVE CLIENT, CR 16.402 -- recorded from the real game and converted to the offline-oracle trace format. Traces: the live corpus, 13 captures, 200096 unit-ticks / 97205 moving ticks. Analysis: the movement pass over the live corpus (Rage, Ice Golem and step arms). WHERE THE MULTIPLIER LIVES: spells_other.csv Rage -> SummonCharacter RageBottle; characters/ragebottle.toml [BUILDING.RageBottle] DeathAreaEffect = 'Rage'; [AEO.Rage] Radius 3000, LifeDuration 4500 ms, BuffTime 1000 ms, CapBuffTimeToAreaEffectTime = true, OnlyOwnTroops = true, Buff = 'Rage'; [BUFF.Rage] SpeedMultiplier = 130. There is no SpeedMultiplier column in area_effect_objects.csv at all -- it is on the BUFF, not the area effect. THE ROUNDING IS FLOOR: the Knight (60 -> 78) and the Skeletons (90 -> 117) are exact products and prove nothing; the RAGED ICE GOLEM does -- its stomped base is 52, 52 * 1.3 = 67.6, and it walks at exactly 67, where round and ceil both give 68. The raged Knight holds S = 78 for t3508..t3563 (56 ticks = 2800 ms) and returns to 60 at t3565, in BOTH clients' captures of the same battle.
BUFF_SPEED_RULE.engine: RECORDED, NOT IMPLEMENTED. royalesim applies no SpeedMultiplier anywhere today, so nothing reads this key yet; path2026.rs `step_delta` takes whatever integer speed it is handed and card.rs `move_speed` documents the rule. When a buff is implemented it must multiply the STOMPED speed and floor.
BUFF_SPEED_RULE.open_composition_order: WHICH OPERAND THE STOMP APPLIES TO IS NOT SETTLED. floor(52 * 130/100) = 67 and floor(floor(45 * 130/100) * 550/470) = floor(58 * 1.17021) = 67 both fit the Ice Golem; only floor(45 * 1.3 * 550/470) = 68 is excluded. A stomp card whose two orderings disagree would settle it.
BUFF_SPEED_RULE.not_this_key: The FREEZE is NOT measured here and must not be quoted from this key. The one Ice Spirit hit in the corpus (frames-auto-20260918-134739, side-1 Knight at (3500, 23499), spirit at t1016) drives the step to exactly zero rather than to a scaled speed, which is consistent with SpeedMultiplier = -100 -- but the Knight retargets the spirit (behavior_state 1 -> 2, path cleared), is pushed 160 native units over 4 ticks, then holds still for 46 ticks = 2300 ms against an 1100 ms BuffTime, and a unit in state 2 does not walk anyway. Nothing in the corpus measures a PARTIAL slow at all. The Prince's ChargeSpeedMultiplier = 200 (ChargeRange 250) is the other buffed speed in the live corpus, at S = 120.
BUFF_SPEED_RULE.promotion_rules: Raise to HIGH with a second non-integral product on a different card, or with any partial slow. Re-open the composition order with a raged stomp card whose two orderings disagree.

STOMP_PAUSE_SCHEDULE.formula: with k the unit's moving-tick index (k = 0 on its first moving tick, NEVER reset), skip the position update iff ((k + 1) * TICK_MS) % (StopMovementAfterMS + WaitMS) > StopMovementAfterMS
STOMP_PAUSE_SCHEDULE.provenance: MEASURED, phase uniquely pinned. OFFLINE TRACE CORPUS (Clash Royale 15.535.29 / versionCode 150535029). Traces: data/oracle-native/{walk (6 cards x 1 deploy), lane_sweep_Knight (128 files / 64 distinct experiments), building_Giant (12), repath_Giant (2), meet (3), orient (1)} -- 150 units, 51926 entity-ticks. Analysis: the offline-oracle passes -- grid, cost model, occlusion and goal rule; every law re-measured over every unit of every trace; timing and the speed law. Report: docs/movement-measurements.md; implementation contract: docs/pathfinder-spec.md. Giant 308/308 and Golem 306/306 moving ticks. Strict > beats >= (304/308, 294/306); (k+1) beats k (268/308, 282/306); every phase offset was brute-forced and only 0 fits. A naive 'move 640 ms then wait 100 ms' countdown gives 13 moving ticks in the Giant's first block and the oracle shows 12.
STOMP_PAUSE_SCHEDULE.scope: The pause gates the unit's OWN LOCOMOTION, not the position write: external displacement still applies during a freeze -- a jostled Giant moves on 2 of 323 scheduled pause ticks.
STOMP_PAUSE_SCHEDULE.what_k_counts_2026_09_18b: `k` ADVANCES ON EVERY LOCOMOTION TICK FROM THE FIRST MOVING TICK, PAUSES INCLUDED. the spec's phrase 'moving-tick index' is ambiguous and the live 16.402 corpus forces this reading: if `k` advanced only on ticks that actually MOVED it would stick at the first pause and the unit would never move again. Under this reading the Ice Golem's pauses are an exact period-11 progression in absolute tick number (Stop 470 + Wait 80 = 550 ms = 11 ticks, runs of 10 moving ticks) and the Giant's are period 740 ms with 13-tick runs. Traces: the live corpus; the movement analysis. VERIFIED IN THE ENGINE, by reading it rather than by assuming it: state.rs `phase_path_2026` increments `kticks[i]` BEFORE the `stomp_paused` test and `continue`s afterwards, so a pause tick still advances the counter. The increment's position is pinned by a comment there.

DEPLOY_TIMING.provenance: MEASURED. OFFLINE TRACE CORPUS (Clash Royale 15.535.29 / versionCode 150535029). Traces: data/oracle-native/{walk (6 cards x 1 deploy), lane_sweep_Knight (128 files / 64 distinct experiments), building_Giant (12), repath_Giant (2), meet (3), orient (1)} -- 150 units, 51926 entity-ticks. CONTACT_DOMAIN.provenance: MEASURED, and this is a statement about what is NOT known. OFFLINE TRACE CORPUS (Clash Royale 15.535.29 / versionCode 150535029). Traces: data/oracle-native/{walk (6 cards x 1 deploy), lane_sweep_Knight (128 files / 64 distinct experiments), building_Giant (12), repath_Giant (2), meet (3), orient (1)} -- 150 units, 51926 entity-ticks. Analysis: the offline-oracle passes -- grid, cost model, occlusion and goal rule; every law re-measured over every unit of every trace; timing and the speed law. Report: docs/movement-measurements.md; implementation contract: docs/pathfinder-spec.md. Three regimes break every law in this section and TWO OF THEM SET NO FLAG AT ALL: avoidance (behavior_state 1, avoidance_offset != 0, heading deflected, |step| within +-2.3 % of S); crowd separation (behavior_state 1, NO flag, |step| about S plus a 15-28 unit lateral residual perpendicular to the heading); combat pushback (behavior_state 2, NO flag, displacement 0.06-2.5 x S, can oppose the heading). 174 flagless failures corpus-wide: 137 at state 1, 36 at state 2, 1 at state 4.
CONTACT_DOMAIN.not_directly_observable: The push is not separately observable in the corpus; it must be inferred from the residual between the predicted and the observed step. Keep it separate from the locomotion law (STOMP_PAUSE_SCHEDULE) so that a pushed unit still moves during a stomp pause. Confirmed again on the live corpus: 1 of 200096 unit-ticks shows anything else.
CONTACT_DOMAIN.how_to_define_isolated_2026_09_18b: 'FREE WALK' MEANS ISOLATED BY DISTANCE, NOT `avoidance_offset == 0`. This is the single easiest way to get a wrong number out of this corpus, and any regression gate written against the flags will look broken on live data for the wrong reason. Offline the traces were single units on an empty board, so the two definitions were the same thing; live they are not, because the corpus records no push of its own AND the separation impulse leaves no flag either. MEASURED on the LIVE 16.402 corpus (the live corpus; the movement analysis, step and push arms): filtering on the fields alone gives step-law exactness 0.7273; adding an isolation radius of 2000 native to the nearest OTHER MOBILE UNIT gives 0.9807; adding Rage and the Prince charge gives 0.99903. Exactness by distance to the nearest other mobile unit -- 0-499: 0.433, 500-999: 0.281, 1000-1499: 0.793, 1500-1999: 0.970, 2000-2499: 0.987, 6000-6499: 0.994. USE d > 2000 native. About 27 % of all live moving ticks are crowded, so no crowded tick can be reproduced bit-exactly until the separation magnitude is fitted.
CONTACT_DOMAIN.what_the_live_pass_refined: Two of the three regimes are better understood, and neither is implemented. AVOIDANCE: on about 11 % of moving ticks (22158 of them) the step is a quantised ROTATION of the pure path heading rather than the heading itself; |step|/S has median 1.0006, so the length is unchanged and only the direction turns. The rotation is monotone in its magnitude and independent of the distance to the node (71.45 deg at d ~ 1082 and 71.60 deg at d ~ 1493 at the largest magnitude seen), so it is a rotation, not a lateral shift of the aim point -- but it is NOT linear (0.256 deg/unit at the smallest magnitude rising to 0.375 deg/unit at the largest; asin(a/256), asin(a*sqrt(2)/256), tan and 1/1024-of-a-turn were all tried and all miss somewhere), and what SETS it is still unknown -- it fires against static occluders too (one Knight of the 2026-09-18 corpus is at the largest magnitude at t3413 with the nearest mobile unit 8315 native away, walking past its own princess tower). SEPARATION: the residual that actually breaks the step law sets none of the three fields; over 24887 off-law ticks with a neighbour inside 1600 native, observed - predicted points AWAY from the nearest neighbour within 7.5 deg on 57.0 % and within 22.5 deg on 65.5 %, and at 180 deg on only 1.3 %, and it fires at a separation peaking exactly at 1.0 x (own CollisionRadius + neighbour CollisionRadius) -- bins 0.9: 4225, 1.0: 11442, 1.1: 4633. The MAGNITUDE is still unfitted (10-unit bins 0: 2893, 10: 3878, 20: 3372, 30: 2782, 40: 2169, 50: 1870, 60: 1668) and no Mass / PushMassFactor term has been tried.
CONTACT_DOMAIN.avoidance_offset: UNVERIFIED, DO NOT GUESS. It is set to +-190 in one tick and then performs a +-10-per-tick walk bounded at +-190 -- 16 of 36 runs ramp back UP before coming down, and runs reach 67 ticks against the 19 a pure decay implies. Do NOT implement 'decremented by 10 per tick toward 0'. What sets it, what selects the sign, and what deflection it applies (the ratio of heading error to offset is 0.327-0.387, non-linear) are all unmeasured.
